newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IFC to raise Hungary Malev capital by $20 mln.
newsitem.headline: IFC to raise Hungary Malev capital by $20 mln.

text.p: The World Bank's International Finance Corporation (IFC) unit is likely to raise Hungarian air carrier Malev's capital by $20 million and to assure loans totalling $60 million to the company, Malev said.
"We have been officially informed from Washington that the World bank approved IFC's planned transaction," Malev CEO Sandor Szathmary told the daily Nepszabadsag on Thursday.
Hungary's government decided recently to start negotiations to repurchase a 30 percent stake in Malev from Alitalia and five percent from the Italian government agency SIMEST.

Alitalia, troubled by financial difficulties, has to sell its stake in Malev according to a European Commission decision, opening the way for Hungary to resume the privatisation of Malev, in which Alitalia bought a stake in 1992.
The government also decided that Malev should raise its registered capital by some $20 million.
Szathmary said IFC planned to raise Malev's registered capital by $20 million and extend a loan of a further $20 million to the airline.
IFC would also help as an intermediator for Malev to access a loan of a further $40 million, he added, without disclosing what the funds would be spent for.

Szathmary added that the state privatisation agency APV was likely to abandon its pre-emption right to buy Alitalia's and SIMEST's stake in favour of a group of Hungarian investors which planned to acquire the shares.
He did not name the investors.
